subject: Recap + proposed acceptance gates for SpireTech POC
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma@spiretech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + proposed acceptance gates for SpireTech POC

Emma / team — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete asks to get the POC kicked off. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Goal of POC (what SpireTech said):
- Validate that Redwood can serve production search/answering traffic for the Recommendations/Search team with predictable latency and acceptable unit cost while maintaining model quality on our extraction tasks.

Proposed scope we discussed:
- Duration: 4 weeks evaluation after a 1–2 week sandbox/setup window.
- Workload: ~synthetic + 10k anonymized query trace replay (you said you can share a 7–14 day slice).
- Primary success dimensions: latency (tail), throughput (sustained), unit cost (USD per token/request), and quality (extraction accuracy / manual eval).

What I need from you to proceed:
1) Confirm you can share the trace leak (anonymized) + a validation set (200 labeled examples) by EOD next Tue (2026-06-23).
2) Decision on SLA: do you need an explicit p95 latency SLA in the POC or just acceptance gates?
3) Any procurement/legal blockers (PO/NDAs) we should fast-track before infra work starts?

Proposed immediate next steps (we can adjust after your replies):
- Redwood: deliver proposed acceptance gates, measurement plan, and a lightweight harness (k8s + sample runner) by Wed (2026-06-24). Attachment: spk-poc-scope.pdf (draft).
- SpireTech: share trace + 200-label set and confirm security contact.
- Kickoff call to schedule: suggest Thu 2026-06-25 10:00 PT — please confirm.

I put Lauren and Ben on Cc to help with measurement definition and cost bounds.

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai
From: Emma Johnson <emma@spiretech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed acceptance gates for SpireTech POC

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. Confirming the high-level scope is correct. A few clarifying points from our side:

- We can deliver a 10k anonymized trace and the 200-label validation set by Tue 2026-06-23 afternoon — security will scrub PII.
- Regarding the SLA: for the POC we don’t need a contract-level SLA, but we do need clear acceptance gates (we'll use them to greenlight a pilot program).
- Quality metrics: for our extraction tasks we'd like to see F1 >= 0.90 and average human helpfulness >= 4.0/5 on a 100-sample blind eval.
- Cost: as a target, our finance team expects a ballpark of <= $0.003 / token for the evaluation budget (we understand final cost may vary by tuning). Can you propose how you'll measure cost/token?

Also: please include a brief risk/migration note for our infra folks — e.g., how we will handle failover/backfill if latency spikes during peak replay.

I can confirm Thu 06/25 10:00 PT for kickoff.

—Emma
Emma Johnson
Head of Search, SpireTech
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Johnson <emma@spiretech.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed acceptance gates for SpireTech POC

Looping in a few measurement notes I think we should include in the draft we send Emma:

Measurement approach (short):
- Latency: collect end-to-end p50/p95/p99 for generation path, measure both cold (no KV cache) and warm (with KV cache) runs. Use the same request size distribution as the shared trace. Report 95th-percentile in ms and show distribution.
- Throughput: run a 10-minute sustained ramp test to define sustained qps; also measure short-burst throughput (30s windows) to simulate traffic spikes.
- Cost: instrument tokens produced + tokens in request; compute USD/token against test cluster pricing (we’ll export cost logs per-route). We should also provide projected cost per 1M requests at observed latencies.
- Quality: run the 200-label validation set + a 100-sample blind manual rating. Quality gates: extraction F1 >= 0.90 AND avg manual rating >= 4.0.

Gates I recommend we propose:
- Gate A (smoke): infra stable, all tests run end-to-end, no PII in data.
- Gate B (performance): p95 <= 150 ms (warm) AND sustained throughput >= 100 req/s for the test workload.
- Gate C (cost/quality): measured unit cost <= $0.0035/token AND quality gates met (F1 + manual rating).

Ownership:
- Redwood infra lead: Ben Carter (measurement harness + cost reports).
- Redwood POC lead: Lauren Bishop (coordination + quality eval).
- SpireTech data/security: Emma Johnson + security contact TBD (for trace handoff).

I’ll fold this into the draft and attach the measurement checklist.

-Lauren
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Johnson <emma@spiretech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed acceptance gates for SpireTech POC

Emma — thanks for the quick turn. Based on Lauren's notes I’ve pulled together the proposed acceptance gates and a practical measurement plan. Attaching a short scope doc (spk-poc-scope.pdf). Highlights below — please review and tell us if any numbers are a non-starter.

Proposed acceptance gates (consolidated):
- Gate A (readiness): dataset received, infra provisioned, smoke tests pass (by 2026-06-28).
- Gate B (performance): p95 latency (warm) <= 150 ms; sustained throughput >= 100 req/s for 10-minute window; no >5% error rate.
- Gate C (quality + cost): extraction F1 >= 0.90 AND avg manual rating >= 4.0/5; measured cost <= $0.0035/token for the evaluation cluster (we'll provide a runbook to instrument this).

Test harness / logistics:
- We'll provide a runner (k8s job + small client) to replay your trace and produce the metrics; Ben will ship a docker image and instructions to your infra team.
- Measurements will be captured into a shared dashboard (Drive link included) and a short runbook will explain how we compute USD/token (tokens counted via canonical tokenizer we use, cost computed from cluster billing exported to per-route cost buckets).

Timeline (proposed):
- Tue 2026-06-23: SpireTech shares trace + 200-labels.
- Wed 2026-06-24: Redwood delivers harness + acceptance gates doc (attached).
- Thu 2026-06-25: Kickoff; sandbox deploy (1–2 days).
- Week of 2026-06-29: Baseline runs + iteration on model/config.
- Week of 2026-07-06: Final acceptance test run and readout.

Open items:
- Risk clause for cost overruns / burst failures — Emma, can you share any internal guardrails we should respect?
- Security contact for the trace handoff.

If that looks good I’ll lock in the kickoff and ask Ben to share the docker image and dashboard link.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: spk-poc-scope.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Emma Johnson <emma@spiretech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed acceptance gates for SpireTech POC

Thanks Karthik / Lauren — this looks great and aligned with our expectations. Two small asks before kickoff:

1) Cost target: finance will accept the $0.0035/token evaluation cap for the POC provided we have a daily spend cap (please propose a default; we suggest $5k/day).
2) Risk clause: include a short paragraph in the scope doc documenting our rollback/backfill approach if latency spikes during replay (we expect Redwood to pause the runner and provide backfill options).

We’ll send the anonymized trace and labels by EOD Tue 06/23 and confirm security contact in the same email. Kickoff 06/25 10:00 PT is confirmed.

—Emma
Head of Search, SpireTech
